mainProgression.description: Bright, uplifting progression anchoring the main melodic theme with strong diatonic movement in G major

sectionProgressions.description: Triumphant I-IV-V-I cadence that establishes the optimistic, soaring character of the piece
Shifts to relative minor starting point, creating a more reflective mood before building back to major resolution

sectionProgressions.progression: G - D/F# - Em - C - D - G
sectionProgressions.romanNumerals: I - V/7 - vi - IV - V - I

harmonicFunction: G (I) - Tonic center establishing bright major tonality and home base for melodic runs
C (IV) - Subdominant providing harmonic lift and contrast to the tonic
D (V) - Dominant creating forward motion and resolution tension back to G
Em (vi) - Relative minor adding emotional depth and melodic minor color
D/F# (V/7) - First inversion dominant creating smooth chromatic bass motion from G to Em

techniques.name: Hybrid Picking
techniques.description: Combining flatpick with middle and ring fingers to execute rapid cascading arpeggios and pentatonic runs that define the signature Cliffs of Dover sound

notes: Pick held between thumb and index finger while middle (m) and ring (a) fingers pluck higher strings
Allows simultaneous bass note attack with pick and treble melody with fingers
Essential for the rapid cross-string pentatonic cascades at 204 BPM
Produces a softer, more violin-like attack on finger-plucked notes compared to pure picking
Eric Johnson uses this to achieve his signature clean-yet-fluid tone across strings
sequence: Anchor pick between thumb and index finger in standard position
Assign middle finger to B string and ring finger to high E string
Practice slow alternation: pick on low strings, fingers on high strings
Build coordination with simple G major pentatonic patterns across 3 strings
Gradually increase speed while maintaining even volume between pick and finger attacks
tips: Start at 50% tempo (around 100 BPM) and build up incrementally
Focus on matching volume between picked and finger-plucked notes
Keep finger movements minimal - pluck from the knuckle, not the whole hand
Practice the cascading G pentatonic pattern in isolation before full song context
Use a clean amp setting to hear every note clearly during practice
details.progression: Pentatonic cascades over G - C - D - Em

techniques.name: Cascading Pentatonic Runs
techniques.description: Rapid descending and ascending pentatonic scale patterns played across multiple string groups, creating the waterfall-like melodic effect that defines the main theme

notes: Based on G major pentatonic positions spanning frets 2-15
Patterns connect multiple pentatonic box positions fluidly
Uses three-note-per-string groupings for speed and fluidity
Combines hammer-ons, pull-offs, and picked notes within single runs
Requires position shifts mid-run without breaking rhythmic flow
sequence: Learn G major pentatonic in all five CAGED positions
Practice connecting adjacent positions with slide transitions
Work three-note-per-string patterns ascending and descending
Add hammer-on/pull-off combinations within each position
Chain positions together into full cascading runs at slow tempo
tips: Memorize the pentatonic patterns as shapes, not individual notes
Use economy picking (directional picking) to minimize pick travel between strings
Let notes ring into each other slightly for the cascading waterfall effect
Practice with compression or light overdrive to hear sustain and note clarity
Record yourself and compare note evenness to the original recording
details.progression: Runs over G major tonal center

techniques.name: Legato Phrasing
techniques.description: Smooth hammer-on and pull-off technique creating a violin-like sustain and fluidity, minimizing pick attack for seamless melodic lines

notes: Emphasizes left-hand strength for clear hammer-ons and pull-offs
Creates the smooth, singing quality of Eric Johnson's melodic statements
Often combined with hybrid picking for mixed articulation within phrases
Used prominently in the lyrical B section and transitional passages
Requires consistent finger pressure to maintain volume across legato passages
sequence: Practice hammer-ons from nothing (tapping the string with fretting finger alone)
Build pull-off strength with chromatic exercises on each string
Work four-note legato patterns: pick first note, hammer-on next three
Apply to G major scale patterns across two octaves
Combine with position shifts for extended legato lines
tips: Develop left-hand finger independence with daily chromatic exercises
Use just enough gain to sustain notes without masking sloppy technique
Focus on making hammer-ons as loud as picked notes
Practice pull-offs with a slight downward flick for better volume
Work the B section melody slowly to internalize the phrasing and breath points
details.progression: Melodic lines over Em - C - G - D

sections.name: Intro - Cascading Theme
sections.description: The iconic opening featuring rapid cascading pentatonic runs that establish the triumphant, soaring character of the piece with hybrid picking across multiple string groups
notes: Cascading pentatonic runs using hybrid picking at full 204 BPM tempo
Three-note-per-string groupings create the signature waterfall effect
Clean tone with slight overdrive and stereo chorus for shimmer
Requires seamless position shifts across the neck without breaking flow

sections.name: Main Theme Statement
sections.description: The primary melodic theme presented with a mix of hybrid picking and legato phrasing, featuring the song's most recognizable melody over the I-IV-V-vi progression
notes: Violin-like tone achieved through neck pickup and touch dynamics
Melodic phrases breathe with natural pauses between statements
Combines picked attack notes with legato hammer-on/pull-off passages
Dynamic swells from soft to loud within individual phrases

sections.name: B Section - Lyrical Passage
sections.description: A more reflective section beginning on the relative minor, featuring extended legato lines and emotive bending with less rhythmic intensity
notes: Shifts emotional tone to relative minor territory
Extended legato phrases with minimal picking for singing quality
Whole-step and half-step bends for expressive vocal-like inflections
Builds gradually in intensity toward return of main theme

sections.name: Climactic Finale
sections.description: The triumphant return and escalation of the main theme, pushing the cascading runs to their most intense and technically demanding peak before the final resolution
sections.progression: G - D/F# - Em - C - D - G
notes: Most technically demanding section with fastest cascading runs
Walking bass descent from G through F# to Em adds harmonic sophistication
Builds to climactic peak before resolving to final G major chord
Requires peak stamina and precision in both hands at full tempo

alternatives: Any high-quality Stratocaster with single-coil pickups
guitar.pickup: Single-coil pickups - neck position for legato, bridge for brighter runs

alternatives: Two-amp setup: Marshall for drive, Fender for clean blend

settings.presence: 7 (airy top end for the violin-like tone)

effects.distortion: Ibanez Tube Screamer TS808 - light gain boost for solo sustain
effects.delay: Maestro Echoplex EP-3 tape delay - subtle slapback for depth
effects.reverb: TC Electronic Stereo Chorus + natural amp reverb for shimmer
effects.other: Stereo chorus is essential for the shimmering clean tone; use sparingly on drive sounds

beginner.focus: Learn the chord progression framework and basic pentatonic positions
steps: Master G major pentatonic in the open position and 2nd position box
Learn the basic G-C-D-Em chord progression as open chords
Practice simple ascending/descending pentatonic runs at slow tempo
Work on basic hybrid picking: pick + middle finger coordination

intermediate.focus: Develop hybrid picking fluency and connect pentatonic positions
steps: Learn all five CAGED pentatonic positions in G major
Practice connecting adjacent positions with slides
Build hybrid picking speed with three-string arpeggio patterns
Learn the main theme melody at 50% speed with correct articulation

advanced.focus: Achieve full-speed execution with musical expression and dynamics
steps: Master cascading runs at 75% tempo (around 150 BPM)
Develop legato strength for the B section melodic passages
Combine hybrid picking with legato within single phrases
Build stamina for the full 3:53 performance at tempo
Refine tone and dynamics to match the original recording

commonMistakes: Attempting to play at full 204 BPM speed before building proper technique
Using all downstrokes or alternate picking instead of hybrid picking for cascading runs
Neglecting the dynamic contrast between loud picked notes and softer legato passages
Playing with too much gain, masking sloppy note articulation in fast runs
Ignoring the musical phrasing and breathing points between melodic statements
practiceRoutine: Warm up with G major pentatonic across all positions for 10 minutes
Hybrid picking coordination drill: pick + middle finger on adjacent strings for 10 minutes
Cascading run patterns at 60% speed with metronome for 15 minutes
Main theme melody practice focusing on dynamics and articulation for 15 minutes
Full section run-throughs at current comfortable speed for 10 minutes
focusAreas: Hybrid picking coordination between flatpick and fingers
Pentatonic position connection and seamless shifting
Left-hand legato strength for hammer-ons and pull-offs
Dynamic control and tone production at high speed
Stamina building for sustained fast passages
metronomeWork: Start cascading runs at 100 BPM (roughly half speed)
Increase by 4-8 BPM increments when current tempo is clean and even
Practice main theme at 120 BPM focusing on articulation clarity
Target 75% speed (150 BPM) as first major milestone
Full tempo (204 BPM) is the final goal - do not rush to reach it
